identity.name: Pathet Lao
native_names: ປະເທດລາວ (Pathet Lao)

land.text: the border provinces of Phongsali and Xam Neua (Houaphan), conquered by the PAVN in April 1953 and left to the Pathet Lao to occupy

predecessors.note: The two provinces were still French Indochina's when the PAVN took them in April 1953; the Kingdom of Laos became independent on 22 October 1953.

land.text: the whole of Laos: the Lao People's Democratic Republic proclaimed on 2 December 1975 with Souphanouvong as President

capitals.name: Xam Neua (Houaphan)
capitals.note: 'Souphanouvong moved the Pathet Lao headquarters into Xam Neua on 19 April' (1953 by the page's paragraph); the Vietnamese established a support group at Ban Nameo in 1954. Vientiane from 23 August 1975.

correction.text: the border provinces of Phongsali and Xam Neua (Houaphan), conquered by the PAVN in April 1953 and left to the Pathet Lao to occupy

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Pathet Lao's solid territory was the two north-eastern provinces from April 1953. The page gives no percentage of land held in 1962, 1970 or 1973, so nothing wider is drawn; the Plain of Jars and the south-east are contested or Vietnamese-occupied (Kingdom of Laos dossier). The coalition years 1957-1959 are left as the same shape (the page says only that a coalition government incorporating the Pathet Lao was established in November 1957).

ledger.note: 1953: the Pathet Lao takes the north-east. In April 1953 the PAVN 'invaded' Phongsali and Xam Neua and 'moved aside to allow the Pathet Lao force ... to occupy the captured ground'; Souphanouvong moved the headquarters into Xam Neua on 19 April.

ledger.note: 1975: the Pathet Lao takes the state (23 August Vientiane; 2 December the monarchy abolished and the Lao People's Democratic Republic proclaimed with Souphanouvong as President).
1975: the movement becomes the state, the Lao People's Democratic Republic (Cliopatria's Communist Laos row, from 1976).

notes: Written as a rebel state by this batch because the Kingdom of Laos dossier needs a counterpart for Phongsali, Houaphan and the Plain of Jars; one page was used. The pages give no list of provinces held by the Pathet Lao in 1960-1962 and no share of the land in later years; a gap-filler should read 'Pathet Lao', 'Neo Lao Hak Xat' and the 'Plain of Jars' articles. The Pathet Lao's own government and the date it became the Lao People's Democratic Republic (2 December 1975) are in the Communist Laos dossier.
